title.en: Compliant spring motion from a restoring force

summary: Drive compliant motion from a restoring force proportional to displacement from a declared rest length, and do not treat a bounce clip as a measured spring.
objective: A linear undamped one-dimensional oscillator moves about its force-balanced equilibrium with amplitude-independent period for positive stiffness and mass.
applies_when: A connector, suspension, or tentacle is meant to restore toward a rest length or angle.
The viewer can change stiffness, mass or amplitude and should see the matching period or rate.
intent_signals: mass on a spring I can tune
example_prompts: Hang a mass from a spring and show that larger pull-back does not change the period under Hooke's law.
Let me stiffen the spring and watch the oscillation get faster.
negative_signals: A squash-and-stretch animation with no rest length.
Engine joint motors presented as laboratory spring constants.
not_for: Plastic yield, rubber hyperelasticity or measured textile stiffness.
A complete cloth model; cloth may use mass-spring networks or other declared formulations.

principles: Distinguish a connector's unloaded natural length from the equilibrium of all forces. A hanging mass shifts the equilibrium under gravity.
For the selected 1D model x is displacement from force-balanced equilibrium, with finite m>0,k>0 and no damping; T=2 pi sqrt(m/k).
An authored bounce or joint controller may be useful but is not a calibrated Hooke spring merely because it looks compliant.
implementation: Own equilibrium, displacement, velocity, m and k. Solve x''=-(k/m)x analytically or with a declared integrator; render stretch from this state.

For an optional spatial connector define d=p_B-p_A, L=|d| and unloaded L0>=0. When L>epsilon, apply F_B=-k(L-L0)d/L and F_A=-F_B, then add other forces such as gravity separately. Reject coincident endpoints at initialization; if L<=epsilon during motion, pause and report the undefined direction instead of normalizing zero.

Period checks belong to the unmodified 1D branch. Force caps or nonlinear limits must be reported as a different model; numerical instability requires a timestep/integration correction rather than an unlabelled force clamp.

If a control allows k=0, disable the finite period readout and set restoring force to zero; existing velocity can persist. Pause preserves velocity and time. Reset restores the initial displacement, velocity, equilibrium and parameters.
observable_checks: Release two finite nonzero amplitudes from rest at fixed positive m,k: the undamped linear periods agree within declared tolerance.
Doubling positive k shortens the linear period by 1/sqrt(2).
At k=0 the restoring acceleration vanishes; motion follows remaining forces and velocity, with no independent periodic mesh writer.

creative_affordances: Coil, leaf or cartoon springs are interchangeable skins on the same rest-length state.
Colouring the spring by stored energy is a free overlay.
known_limits: OpenStax SHM assumes Hooke's law and no damping; real springs leave that regime at large strain.
Explicit integrators become unstable as k grows; that is a numerical limit, not a material one.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact has been observed for this record.

claims.statement: Simple harmonic motion occurs when the net force obeys Hooke's law F_s = -k x with no damping; the period and frequency then depend on mass and the force constant and are independent of amplitude.
claims.scope: One-dimensional linear undamped oscillator with finite m,k>0 and x measured from force-balanced equilibrium; not a period guarantee for spatial networks or plastic materials.

source_refs.locator: 15.1, Equations of SHM and Eq15.7; Figure15.10 hanging spring and shifted equilibrium
